content: The UCSD Medical Center is a prominent research hospital situated in the Hillcrest neighborhood of San Diego, California. Together with the UCSD Thornton Hospital in La Jolla, it serves as the primary teaching facility for the UC San Diego School of Medicine and the School of Pharmacy. The Hillcrest Center has 386 beds, while the UCSD Thornton Hospital has 119 beds, forming the core of the UCSD Medical Center. Specialized facilities include the Shiley Eye Center, the Moores Cancer Center, and the Trauma Center in Hillcrest. Notably, the Moores Cancer Center is the only comprehensive cancer center in the region, and the Hillcrest Trauma Center is one of only two Level I Trauma Centers in the area, the other being Scripps Mercy Hospital. The UCSD Medical Center is highly esteemed for its significant contributions to healthcare in San Diego. In 2007, it was recognized by US News and World Report as one of the best hospitals in the nation in six specialty areas, ranking 8th in respiratory disorders, 18th in rheumatology, 30th in kidney disease, 30th in gynecology, 39th in cancer, and 50th in ear, nose, and throat care. The UCSD Medical Center in Hillcrest is the primary hospital for the University of California, San Diego School of Medicine. As the region's only academic medical center, it provides both primary care and specialized services, including comprehensive surgical care, genetic disease diagnosis and management, neurology, orthopedics, oncology, and sleep medicine. The recently renovated 386-bed hospital also serves as the main site for several regional programs, such as the Comprehensive Organ Transplant Program, Bone Marrow Transplantation, the San Diego Regional Burn Center, the Infant Special Care Center (NICU), UCSD's Birth Center, San Diego County's only Level I Trauma Center, and the National Institutes of Health-Designated Clinical Research Center. The John M. and Sally B. Thornton Hospital, part of UCSD, is a 119-bed medical-surgical facility that opened in the summer of 1993. It offers a wide range of services, including surgery, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, orthopedics, oncology, reproductive medicine, and pulmonary medicine. The hospital is also home to the Perlman Ambulatory Care Center. The Rebecca and John Moores UCSD Cancer Center, established in 1979, is one of only 39 National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers in the United States. These centers are recognized for their leadership in scientific innovation and clinical excellence. The Moores Cancer Center is the only Comprehensive Cancer Center in San Diego and Imperial counties to have achieved this distinction. In 2007, the UCSD Medical Center was ranked 39th in the nation for cancer treatment by US News and World Report. The UCSD Shiley Eye Center provides exceptional eye care for patients of all ages, ranging from routine eye exams to advanced diagnostic procedures and complex surgeries. The center offers a comprehensive array of services, including cataract surgery, corneal transplants, glaucoma diagnosis and treatment, low vision services, neuro-ophthalmology, optometry and contact lens services, pediatric ophthalmology, plastic surgery, refractive surgery, retina care, and trauma repair. Adjacent to the Shiley Eye Center is the Abraham Ratner Children's Eye Center, the only dedicated pediatric eye care facility in the San Diego region, designed to address the unique vision needs of children. On May 18, 2007, the UC Regents approved a plan to construct an additional inpatient tower in La Jolla, which will house 125 to 150 beds.
